items.title: AI Has Entered the Boardroom. Who’s Overseeing It? | Stanford Graduate School of Business
items.summary:
In the survey, 75% of directors said they used AI for research and market analysis, 55% for board prep and material summarization. Other common uses included strategic question generation and competitive benchmarking. Matthys says that board members would ideally like to use AI “to track and summarize board packages and more quickly understand year-to-year trends by using LLM tools rather than reading 80- to 100-page reports.” [...] The sooner the better, the researchers suggest. “Moving too slowly with AI governance means you may miss out on opportunities,” Saripalli says. “The board has fiduciary responsibility for anything that has impact at the product or service level.”

“The risk of not moving is as serious as the risk of AI systems running amok,” Matthys adds, noting how past technological shifts have left unprepared companies behind. “If you don’t keep up, there’s a risk that 20 years from now you won’t exist.” [...] ## In Brief

 A new survey finds that corporate boards are not keeping up with AI governance.
 Directors report that they are discussing and using AI, yet their boards lack a systematic approach to oversight.
 Companies that wait to define AI strategy and audit their AI use risk being left behind.

“We’re trying to change the wheels on the bus while driving it at 100 miles an hour downhill.”

items.title: Chapman Advances Healthcare AI Research and Training | Chapman Newsroom
items.summary:
Totonchy sees the skepticism around AI in higher education as an opportunity.  

“Generative AI quickly gained a negative reputation because it was seen as a tool for cheating,” she said. “That misses the point. These tools can work alongside humans, handling routine tasks so people can focus on analysis and decision-making. The sooner institutions move past resistance, the sooner AI can support that work.” 

STUDENTS PUT AI TO WORK [...] To address bias in clinical decision-making tools, Wang founded the Healthcare AI Initiative (HAI) at Chapman, bringing together researchers working on pressing healthcare challenges. HAI examines ethical questions surrounding AI, including data privacy, and develops equitable machine learning approaches.  

Wang also developed an AI elective within the School of Pharmacy, focused on practical applications for future clinicians. [...] “Every pharmacist has heard the rumors that AI will take pharmacists’ jobs,” Wang said. “But early exposure helps students. As future clinicians, they learn where the real focus should be in relation to AI. That’s something my students learn in this course.”  

Wang also works with students on research projects, extending that learning beyond the classroom. Two PharmD students, Elena Wu ’27 and Harvey Duong ’27, have collaborated with her on studies using AI to analyze large datasets.

items.title: Hochul cites Democratic control of Congress in pushing AI regulation, federal dollars
items.summary:
She’s likely to lean on Schumer and Jeffries, who are angling for leadership positions. Jeffries stumped for her on the eve of Election Day.

Though there are dozens of competing AI-enforcement bills currently floating around Capitol Hill, the governor says Congress should adopt New York’s Responsible AI Safety and Education Act.

The law takes effect on Jan. 1 and is set to force big AI companies to publish specific safety protocols — or else face civil penalties. [...] Hochul says she will use her relationships with New York Democrats in Washington to speed up artificial intelligence regulations — a sharp contrast from a lack thereof under the current congressional makeup and roadblocks by the Trump administration.

“When they start looking for ways to regulate AI, the first place they should look is New York. Because we are building a national model for smart, sensible AI regulation,” Hochul said. [...] So far, the Hochul administration says at least two companies have agreed to sign on, but declined to say which ones.

“We evolve as the threats grow bigger and bigger. We were concerned about social media and the addictive algorithms on children two years ago,” Hochul said.

“Now, we have to do something even more dramatic than we had done last year with signing the RAISE ACT. Unfortunately, we’re in a place of ‘catch up all the time,’” she added.

items.title: As AI stakes its claim in higher education, colleges and universities across Chicago aim to embrace it - CCC
items.summary: “We cannot shy away from this technology. We can’t bury our heads in the sand or anything like that,” Potter said. “We need to ensure that our students have AI competencies, and part of that is responsible use of AI and ethical use of AI, and so that’s the position that we started out with, and that we are still carrying forward to this day.” [...] The degree is applicable and relevant across all disciplines, from history and law to transportation and distribution, City Colleges’ Provost and Chief Academic Officer Mark Potter told the Tribune. He added that before the new program, City Colleges created a district-wide AI steering committee that helped hone and articulate the school’s position on AI: Preparing students for an AI-enabled workforce and society is essential. [...] Across the schools of City Colleges of Chicago, which serves more than 73,000 students a year through its network of multiple public community colleges, AI is being considered widely. The system introduced its first AI degree program at Wilbur Wright College this fall, and students can now earn an Associate of Applied Science degree in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Development.

items.title: The Archbishop of San Francisco on Staying Human in the AI Age
items.summary:
READ IN APP

As archbishop of San Francisco, I serve in the city where some of the world’s most powerful AI systems are being developed. The people building them are making decisions that will shape how billions of us live. In my conversations with some of these developers, I’ve been struck by their concern about the dangers of the technology they’re creating—and perhaps more surprisingly, their willingness to turn to the Catholic Church for moral guidance. [...] The Free Press

ForumNewslettersSign InSubscribe

The Archbishop of San Francisco on Staying Human in the AI Age

Archbishop Salvatore Cordileone leads the prayer of commendation during the funeral Mass of archbishop emeritus and Cardinal William Joseph Cardinal Levada on October 24, 2019, in San Francisco. (Liz Hafalia/San Francisco Chronicle via AP)

Whether AI serves humanity will depend less on the brilliance of its builders than on their virtue.

By Archbishop Salvatore Cordileone [...] is the first major teaching document of his papacy, devoted to a single question: how to safeguard the human person in the age of AI.

items.title: Hỗ trợ doanh nghiệp ứng dụng công nghệ, nâng cao sức cạnh tranh
items.summary: Tiến sĩ Chu Thúc Đạt, Phó Cục trưởng Cục Đổi mới sáng tạo (Bộ Khoa học và Công nghệ) cho biết, trong bối cảnh cạnh tranh ngày càng gay gắt, năng lực công nghệ có vai trò quan trọng, trực tiếp ảnh hưởng đến năng suất, chất lượng sản phẩm, hiệu quả sử dụng nguyên liệu và khả năng tham gia chuỗi giá trị của doanh nghiệp ngành chế biến, chế tạo. Trên cơ sở Chương trình phối hợp giai đoạn 2026 - 2030 với định hướng thúc đẩy khoa học, công nghệ và đổi mới sáng tạo gắn với các chuỗi giá trị ngành hàng [...] Chia sẻ về thực tiễn ứng dụng công nghệ vào sản xuất, Phó Giám đốc Công ty Trách nhiệm hữu hạn Sản xuất thương mại Phước Thành IV  Huỳnh Hồng Thắm cho biết, công ty đang đề xuất tiếp cận công nghệ chế biến khoai lang tím nhằm đa dạng hóa đầu ra, gắn sản phẩm chế biến với nhu cầu thị trường và người tiêu dùng. Với nền tảng công nghệ sẵn có trong lĩnh vực chế biến, kinh doanh gạo, đóng gói bao bì, cùng kinh nghiệm cải tiến quy trình sản xuất, công ty có điều kiện tiếp nhận, ứng dụng công nghệ mới [...] giá trị ngành hàng chủ lực, hội thảo là dịp để cụ thể hóa các nội dung phối hợp thông qua việc xác định nhu cầu công nghệ của doanh nghiệp, kết nối với các giải pháp phù hợp và huy động nguồn lực hỗ trợ triển khai vào thực tiễn sản xuất.

results.input: Giải giúp mình bài toán tích phân: nguyên hàm của x^2 là gì?

result.actual_text:
Để tìm nguyên hàm (tích phân bất định) của \(x^{2}\), ta áp dụng công thức cơ bản:

\[
\int x^{n}\,dx = \frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1} + C \qquad (n \neq -1)
\]

Với \(n = 2\):

\[
\int x^{2}\,dx = \frac{x^{2+1}}{2+1} + C = \frac{x^{3}}{3} + C
\]

Vậy nguyên hàm của \(x^{2}\) là \(\displaystyle \frac{x^{3}}{3} + C\), trong đó \(C\) là hằng số tùy ý.

result.actual_text:
Tôi là một trợ lý nghiên cứu thông minh, được thiết kế để giúp bạn tìm kiếm thông tin, tổng hợp tin tức, khám phá các bài viết trên mạng xã hội, đọc và tóm tắt nội dung từ các liên kết web, tra cứu thời tiết, và thậm chí chuẩn bị các bản tóm tắt dạng markdown.  

**Các khả năng chính của tôi bao gồm:**

- **Tìm tin tức và thông tin chung** trên web (dùng công cụ `lookup`).  
- **Tìm và lấy các bài đăng trên X/Twitter** theo từ khóa hoặc theo tài khoản cụ thể (dùng `social_search` hoặc `timeline`).  
- **Đọc và tóm tắt nội dung từ một URL** mà bạn cung cấp (dùng `fetch`).  
- **Tra cứu thời tiết hiện tại và dự báo** cho các thành phố trên thế giới (dùng `weather`).  
- **Tìm kiếm và trích xuất các bài báo khoa học** trên arXiv (dùng `papers` và `paper_text`).  
- **Định dạng các kết quả nghiên cứu** thành bản tóm tắt markdown có cấu trúc (dùng `format`).  
- **Gửi tin nhắn** hoặc bản tin đã chuẩn bị lên kênh Telegram của bạn (sau khi bạn xác nhận).  

Tôi luôn cố gắng cung cấp thông tin chính xác, cập nhật và phù hợp với yêu cầu của bạn, đồng thời tuân thủ các quy tắc bảo mật và quyền riêng tư. Nếu bạn có bất kỳ yêu cầu nào, chỉ cần cho tôi biết chi tiết, tôi sẽ hỗ trợ ngay!

results.input: Viết giúp mình một hàm Python tính Fibonacci bằng recursion.

result.actual_text:
Dưới đây là một hàm Python đơn giản tính số Fibonacci thứ n bằng đệ quy (recursion). Hàm sẽ trả về giá trị `F(n)` với `F(0) = 0`, `F(1) = 1` và `F(n) = F(n‑1) + F(n‑2)` cho `n ≥ 2`.

```python
def fibonacci(n: int) -> int:
    """
    Tính số Fibonacci thứ n bằng đệ quy.

    Tham số:
        n (int): Chỉ số của số Fibonacci cần tính (n >= 0).

    Trả về:
        int: Giá trị Fibonacci tương ứng.
    """
    if n < 0:
        raise ValueError("Chỉ số n phải là số nguyên không âm")
    if n == 0:
        return 0
    if n == 1:
        return 1
    # Đệ quy: F(n) = F(n-1) + F(n-2)
    return fibonacci(n - 1) + fibonacci(n - 2)


# Ví dụ sử dụng
if __name__ == "__main__":
    for i in range(10):
        print(f"F({i}) = {fibonacci(i)}")
```

**Giải thích nhanh:**
- Hàm kiểm tra các trường hợp cơ bản (`n == 0` và `n == 1`) để dừng đệ quy.
- Đối với các giá trị lớn hơn, hàm gọi lại chính nó với `n-1` và `n-2`, sau đó cộng kết quả lại.
- Lưu ý: Đệ quy thuần như trên có độ phức tạp thời gian O(2ⁿ) và sẽ chậm đối với `n` lớn. Nếu cần tính nhanh hơn, bạn có thể dùng memoization hoặc chuyển sang thuật toán lặp.

items.title: How Robots are Delivering ROI in Mexico?
items.summary:
Articulated robots: Multi-axis robotic arms used for welding, painting, assembly, and heavy material handling. They remain particularly relevant to automotive production.
 SCARA robots: Systems designed for high-speed, precise horizontal movements, frequently used in electronics assembly, component insertion, and packaging.
 Delta robots: Parallel-arm systems suited to rapid picking, sorting, and packaging, particularly in food and consumer goods manufacturing. [...] However, the evolution of industrial robotics is changing the investment equation. Historically, manufacturers deployed robots primarily for repetitive, high-volume operations, including welding vehicle bodies, painting components, and transferring materials between production stations. Modern systems increasingly combine robotic manipulators with machine vision, sensors, AI, and software that allows manufacturers to change production parameters without rebuilding entire automation systems. [...] The most commercially established applications in Mexico are articulated industrial arms, particularly those deployed in welding, painting, assembly, and material handling. These systems can operate continuously, execute repetitive movements with consistent precision, and integrate into production lines. Their adoption is especially relevant to automotive manufacturers, where production volumes and quality requirements can justify substantial capital expenditure.

items.title: Gemini Robotics 2.5: Accelerating Physical Intelligence — Google DeepMind
items.summary:
Dexterity: Our robots can perform significantly more tasks with greater performance and dexterity — from using everyday tools to handling delicate, flexible objects.
 Reliability: During a real-world proof-of-concept on Mercedes-Benz production lines, our models helped Apptronik’s Apollo 2 humanoid pick and pack automotive parts with a 96% success rate. This could enable robots to take on monotonous work, to enable technicians to focus on complex build tasks. [...] Robots struggle to adapt to new unpredictable environments, our Gemini Robotics models give Apollo the ability to think, reason over multiple steps, and take action adapting to changes. In this proof-of-concept, Apollo 2 autonomously performs automotive kitting: the repetitive, physically taxing task of sorting individual parts from bulk bins into organized trays in the exact order needed for each vehicle on the line. Offloading this monotonous prep work helps keep the assembly line moving, [...] With Gemini Robotics 2.5, we expanded the model capabilities in task breadth, performance, and complexity. We evaluated the model across 200 distinct tasks — such as serving food with tongs, tying a bow on a gift box, and pipetting a liquid. These tasks represent a step toward human-level dexterity by combining a number of skills, including advanced tool use, complex manipulation of deformables, and handling delicate objects with finesse.
